mentalModelCheck.question: Why MUST xmpp_stream_parser call binary:copy/1 when extracting stanza attributes from TCP chunks?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
<<Header:10/binary, User:4/binary, Rest/binary>> = PacketBin,
%% Storing User into persistent session state

options.label: Without binary:copy/1, the 4-byte slice pins the entire 64KB off-heap ProcBin in memory, preventing GC from freeing it.
options.explanation: Correct! BEAM reference-counted binaries (>64 bytes) cannot be freed until all sub-binary slices are GC-collected. Calling binary:copy/1 forces a local heap copy, unpinning the 64KB TCP buffer.

options.label: Binary slices cannot be matched with Erlang pattern matching without copying.
options.explanation: Binary pattern matching works natively on slices without copying.

options.label: binary:copy/1 encrypts the binary before storing it in the ETS table.
options.explanation: binary:copy/1 merely copies the binary bytes into fresh unreferenced memory.
